heading: Questions? We can read your mind

items.q: Is a BBA in finance a good degree?
a: Yes. The BBA Finance at ATLAS ISME is UGC-recognised and industry-endorsed, with a curriculum built around live projects, business simulations and CXO-led masterclasses, making it a strong foundation for careers in banking, investment and corporate finance.

items.q: What is the scope of BBA in Finance?
a: Graduates can pursue roles such as Financial Analyst, Investment Banker, Portfolio Manager, Credit Analyst and Business Development Manager, across MNCs, financial services firms, start-ups and entrepreneurial ventures.

items.q: Which is best, BBA or BBA Finance?
a: A general BBA gives you a broad business foundation, while BBA Finance offers a sharper, role-specific focus. If you have a clear interest in capital markets, investment or corporate finance, the BBA Finance is the more targeted and career-ready choice.

items.q: Is BBA finance difficult?
a: It's rigorous but structured well. Concepts like financial modelling, investment analysis and risk management require quantitative thinking, but ATLAS ISME's industry-integrated teaching methodology uses case studies, simulations and live projects to make learning applied and progressive.

items.q: Which finance degree is best?
a: At ATLAS ISME, the BBA (Hons.) in Finance suits those wanting a broader business + finance combination. The B.Sc. (Hons.) in Finance is CFA-curriculum aligned and ideal for those targeting pure finance careers in investment banking, wealth management or global markets.

items.q: Which college is best for BBA in finance?
a: ATLAS ISME is a strong choice. Located in Mumbai's BKC, it works with the dynamic business industry surrounding the campus to create opportunities like masterclasses, global immersions, internships and industry mentorship, all within walking distance of 500+ corporations.

items.q: What core subjects are in a BBA in Finance?
a: Key subjects include Corporate Finance, Investment Analysis & Portfolio Management and Financial Modelling. The curriculum also covers Financial Statement Analysis, Business Law, Statistics for Business, Derivatives & Risk Management, FinTech & Blockchain in Finance and Alternative Investments.

items.q: Do I need maths for BBA finance?
a: For the BBA Finance major, the standard eligibility is 50% in Class XII in any stream; Maths is not mandatory. However, for the B.Sc. (Hons.) in Finance, Mathematics is a mandatory subject with a minimum of 60%.

items.q: Is BBA Finance better than B.Com?
a: BBA Finance at ATLAS ISME is more practice-oriented compared to a traditional B.Com that leans toward accounting and compliance. If you want real-world financial thinking over theory, BBA Finance is the stronger pick.

items.q: Can I pursue CFA after BBA Finance?
a: Yes. ATLAS ISME provides on-campus CFA exam coaching, with modules designed around case studies and industry notes to prepare students thoroughly. The B.Sc. Finance program is also CFA curriculum aligned, making it an even stronger launchpad.

items.q: Which industries hire BBA Finance graduates?
a: Graduates are hired across banking, investment management, corporate finance, fintech, consulting, private equity, wealth management and insurance, with ATLAS ISME alumni placed at leading Indian and global firms.

items.q: What skills are needed for a career in finance after a BBA?
a: Key skills include financial modelling, valuation, data interpretation, analytical thinking and communication. ATLAS ISME builds these through live market labs, investment challenges, financial simulations and mandatory internships, ensuring students are industry-ready from day one.

items.q: Is it good to minor in economics?
a: Yes, especially if your major is in a business or strategy-oriented field. The Economics minor at ATLAS ISME helps students explore the economic forces and policies shaping global businesses and markets and learn how economic analysis informs decision-making and drives innovation through public policy. It adds analytical depth and macro-level thinking that directly complements any business major.

items.q: What is a minor subject in BBA?
a: At ATLAS ISME, a minor is a secondary area of specialisation you study alongside your chosen major. The BBA / BBA (Hons.) program is designed in two steps allowing you to design a business education that's as dynamic as the world you're entering. Minors available include Marketing, Finance, Business Analytics, Entrepreneurship, Economics, AI & Emerging Technologies, Digital Branding & Advertising and Business Psychology.

items.q: Is BBA possible without economics?
a: Yes. Economics is not a mandatory standalone subject in the BBA at ATLAS ISME, it is an optional Minor you can choose to add to your degree. If you select a different Minor (such as Finance or Business Analytics), you can still complete your BBA without any Economics coursework. However, a foundational Economics course does appear in the core curriculum as part of the broader business foundation.

items.q: Is BBA better or economics?
a: They serve different purposes. A BBA is a professional, practice-oriented degree focused on business management, strategy and career readiness across corporate roles. A pure Economics degree is more analytical and research-oriented. At ATLAS ISME, the BBA with an Economics Minor gives you the best of both without committing to a full Economics degree.

items.q: Is economics very math heavy?
a: At ATLAS ISME, the Economics Minor within the BBA is applied rather than purely mathematical. Subjects include Microeconomic Analysis, Macroeconomic Analysis, Quantitative Methods for Economics, Economic Analysis of Public Policy, International Economics, Development Economics, Behavioural Economics, Game Theory & Strategic Thinking, Environmental & Sustainability Economics and Econometrics & Data Analytics. While some quantitative thinking is involved, the emphasis is on real-world application and business relevance, not advanced pure mathematics.

items.q: What are the subjects in BBA economics?
a: The Economics Minor across the BBA in Marketing curriculum includes: Economics (foundational), Microeconomic Analysis, Macroeconomic Analysis, Quantitative Methods for Economics, Economic Analysis of Public Policy, International Economics, Development Economics, Behavioural Economics, Game Theory & Strategic Thinking, Environmental & Sustainability Economics and Econometrics & Data Analytics.

items.q: Why should a Marketing student choose Economics as a Minor?
a: Economics gives Marketing students a powerful analytical edge. Understanding consumer demand, pricing dynamics, market competition and macroeconomic trends helps marketers build smarter strategies, not just creative ones. Subjects like Behavioural Economics and Game Theory directly enhance how a marketer understands consumer decision-making and competitor behaviour, while Econometrics & Data Analytics adds a quantitative layer to campaign and market analysis.

items.q: How does an Economics Minor enhance career opportunities for students?
a: The Economics Minor equips you with analytical and quantitative skills, helping you understand market trends, economic policies and business environments. This opens doors to roles in market research, economic consulting, policy advisory, finance and strategy. Combining economic insight with your major makes you a well-rounded candidate, giving you an edge in placements and making you highly attractive to recruiters across corporates, start-ups and research institutions.

items.q: Does the Minor in Economics appear on my degree certificate?
a: The website does not specify this directly. It is advisable to confirm with the ATLAS ISME Admissions or Academic team for the exact degree nomenclature. However, at most universities following the NEP framework both the Major and Minor are reflected in the academic transcript and degree documentation.
